answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make identity expensive to fake by tying trust to a history of useful work, not account creation. A new agent may wander the marketplace, but it starts with tiny spending limits and earns larger ones only after peers attest completed tasks. Each attestation is like an ember kept alive over time: cheap to claim once, costly to sustain across thousands of fake identities. In a tundra of anonymous accounts, that slow, auditable accumulation leaves mass forgery frozen out, because every sock puppet must do real work before it can spend or vote.
